paper.title: ReCreate: Reasoning and Creating Domain Agents Driven by Experience
paper.central_claim: ReCreate, an agent-as-optimizer that inspects task-agent interaction experience (trajectories, execution and evaluation results, environment) and edits the task agent's scaffold (prompts, workflow, tools, memory) with instance-level proposals consolidated into domain-level updates, creates domain agents from minimal seed scaffolds that outperform human-designed, self-evolving and automated-agent-generation baselines across thirteen settings in four domains at lower optimization cost than ADAS.

sections_read: 5 experiments (5.1-5.7, Tables 1-2, Figures 4-8 captions and prose)

Appendix A-M (usage of LLMs, related work, discussion, implementation, scaffold-gap study, dataset counts and splits, temperature, generalization, significance, sensitivity, motivation cases, ReCreate-Agent and synthesis prompts, Django seed/final scaffold)

evidence.quote: we introduce an agent-as-optimizer paradigm in which an optimizer agent actively inspects execution experience and iteratively refines the task agent’s scaffold
evidence.support_explanation: Central operation: an agent (not a scalar-score loop) diagnoses from experience and edits the non-weight scaffold.

evidence.quote: Each candidate scaffold typically requires large-scale evaluation to yield a stable and reliable performance measure.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap part 2: metric-driven scaffold search is costly; part 1 is that scalar metrics give no why/how evidence (ADAS ~$500 for one ARC generation is cited).

evidence.quote: These search-based methods operate over increasingly rich design spaces but still rely on coarse scalar scores, without explicitly reasoning over the interaction experience when updating scaffold.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest neighbors named: ADAS, AFlow, AgentSquare, AgentSwift, ScoreFlow, RobustFlow, FlowReasoner; positioned as metric-only.

evidence.quote: Another line treats memory as an experience library by summarizing interaction history into reusable guidance
evidence.support_explanation: Trajectory-using self-evolving neighbors exist (ExpeL, AWM, SCOPE, Live-SWE-Agent), so 'metric-only' is not a fair description of all baselines; the delta is fine-grained on-demand inspection plus multi-component scaffold editing.

evidence.quote: You are an agent that creates and evolves other AI agents by editing their scaffolds (prompts, workflows, tools, and memory mechanisms).
evidence.support_explanation: Edit object: non-weight scaffold components (system_template, instance_template, memory_template, agent_tools/, agent_memory/).

evidence.quote: which are buffered rather than immediately applied.
evidence.support_explanation: Instance-level proposals are buffered, then synthesized into a domain-level update (DomUpd).

evidence.quote: This hierarchical process filters out task-specific noise, ensuring that only generalized updates are integrated into the final domain agent scaffold.
evidence.support_explanation: Filtering is performed by an LLM synthesis step, not by a measured admission test; 'ensuring' is an assertion.

evidence.quote: Prefer changes supported by multiple instances; otherwise choose the simpler, more general formulation. When uncertain, keep the original rule.
evidence.support_explanation: Conflict/uncertainty handling is a prompt instruction; no re-run of the candidate scaffold on dev before adoption is described.

evidence.quote: enabling reproducible comparisons to the baseline scaffold.
evidence.support_explanation: Sentence closes the description that each batch's global scaffold is stored as versioned folders global_v000, global_v001, ... with diffs, i.e., versions exist but no rollback rule is stated.

evidence.quote: The agent only preloads lightweight metadata, and lazily reads the full instructions or runs scripts on demand, enabling many tools without saturating the context window.
evidence.support_explanation: Next-run reading mechanism for created tools (SKILL.md-style directories).

evidence.quote: The memory mechanism specifies when the task agent should write new memories and when it should retrieve existing memories (e.g., after repeated failures or before critical steps), making memory usage a controlled part of the workflow.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory component: read/write timing plus a static bank written by the optimizer; no online update or expiry of the bank.

evidence.quote: as the ReCreate-Agent to guarantee high-quality reasoning and scaffold updates.
evidence.support_explanation: Optimizer is claude-4.5-opus while the task agent is gpt-5-mini; improver is a frozen stronger model.

evidence.quote: for each domain, reserving all remaining data for testing (ranging from
evidence.support_explanation: ~20 dev instances per domain for scaffold creation; remaining data (38-417) held out for testing.

evidence.quote: In our experiments, we use AIME24 as the development set and evaluate on the MATH500 topic subsets as test sets.
evidence.support_explanation: Math dev and test come from different benchmarks, a stronger separation than the other domains.

evidence.quote: ReCreate consistently exceeds both human-designed scaffolds and self-evolving baselines across all domains.
evidence.support_explanation: Main claim; Table 1 average row: ReCreate 66.15 vs ExpeL 60.62, LIVE 60.57, SBA 60.05, Refine 59.54, CoT 59.29, OPRO 58.99, AgentSquare 58.62, ADAS 55.60 (gpt-5-mini task agent, single reported number per cell).

evidence.quote: Pass rate or testing score on various real-world agent benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 cells are single numbers; Digital (AppWorld) and several DS subsets have 38-75 test items, so some per-dataset margins are within sampling noise.

evidence.quote: Among the variants, removing the full trajectory causes the largest and most consistent performance drop
evidence.support_explanation: Trajectory/experience-component ablations (Figure 5) support the claim that trace evidence matters; numbers are in the figure only.

evidence.quote: consistently hurts the performance across SWE, DA-Code, and DS-1000 (DS for short).
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2: full 60.19/39.77/77.74 vs w/o creation router 58.00/37.13/75.39 vs w/o DomUpd 57.09/37.83/75.96; 2-3 point drops, single run.

evidence.quote: Second, ReCreate with Claude-opus consistently surpasses Human-designed scaffolds, whereas ReCreate with gpt-5-mini fails to outperform them in most domains.
evidence.support_explanation: The method's gain depends on a strong optimizer model; it does not show that the experience-driven design, rather than optimizer strength, explains the margin over baselines whose optimizer model is unspecified.

evidence.quote: First, ReCreate with only initial domain information yields very poor performance in most domains (except Math).
evidence.support_explanation: Seed-scaffold-only control (Figure 6): evolution from experience is what lifts performance; numbers are in a radar figure.

evidence.quote: The second category is Self-Evolving methods, where agents autonomously refine themselves for solving tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines LIVE, OPRO, ExpeL, ADAS, AgentSquare are described by category only; which LLM drives their optimization, their dev sets and budgets are not stated.

evidence.quote: we conduct McNemar paired significance tests on all test instances across 13 datasets (N=1681).
evidence.support_explanation: Table 5: exact p 3.4e-11 vs SBA, 7.6e-8 vs ExpeL, 9.2e-11 vs AgentSquare; pooled over datasets, treats the created scaffold as fixed, and the AgentSquare row is used as best of the generation category although ADAS is the cost baseline.

evidence.quote: It can be observed that ReCreate maintains comparable performance across different sampling temperatures.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 4 averages 65.66/64.97/65.74 are stable but individual datasets swing widely (e.g., DA-Code ML 40.88/51.16/45.78, Matplotlib 85.19/78.52/74.07), evidencing high creation-run variance per dataset.

evidence.quote: Even with different dev-set samples, performance remains stable (std = 0.28)
evidence.support_explanation: Three 50-instance dev sets sampled from SWE-bench Full excluding Verified; SWE only; dev size 20/50/100 gives 57.4/60.4/60.8.

evidence.quote: We conclude that the performance of ReCreate improves as the dev set size increases.
evidence.support_explanation: Dev size matters (57.4 at 20 vs 60.8 at 100) and the main results use 20.

evidence.locator: App. H Generalization on Various Models
evidence.quote: These results indicate that ReCreate’s experience-driven scaffold edits capture largely model-agnostic role/process/tool/memory patterns rather than backbone-specific prompt tricks.
evidence.support_explanation: Swapping the task agent to Gemini-2.5-Flash / GPT-4o-mini (+8.3/+8.7 points over human-designed, 12/13 and 13/13 tasks) is a transfer check, but the scaffold is re-created per backbone per the text, not transferred; figure-only numbers.

evidence.quote: In contrast, ADAS has to repeatedly evaluate each candidate, leading to higher cost.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost comparison (Figure 8, 36%-82% lower than ADAS) is against ADAS only; ReCreate's own spend with claude-4.5-opus is not tabulated in text and no other baseline's cost is given.

evidence.quote: Under this setting, ReCreate steadily improves both the task’s resolved rate and its test-case pass rate by iteratively updating the agent scaffold.
evidence.support_explanation: Single-case dev sets re-evaluated on the same case; shows the update can fix a failing task, not generalization.

evidence.quote: ReCreate does not update base model parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms the non-weight scope; harness/environment adaptation is also excluded by the authors.

evidence.quote: On Django, the agent heavily inspects the Docker sandbox for code base, while creation mainly manifests as memory construction to consolidate debugging findings into reusable rules.
evidence.support_explanation: Edit-type distribution is domain-dependent and, in the Django case, is mostly memory rather than tools or prompts; no per-edit-type ablation tells which retained artifact carries the gain.

signatures.object: Task-agent scaffold: system_template (role), instance_template (workflow), memory_template, agent_tools/ (SKILL.md-style tool folders), agent_memory/ (static bank); baseline is a minimal seed scaffold
signatures.information: ReCreate-Agent sees the current scaffold, full trajectory, execution and verifier results, and Docker environment state of dev tasks via an evidence retriever and inspection tools; test tasks are not visible
signatures.operation: Per dev instance the optimizer inspects evidence, routes via a creation router to a component and emits a scaffold diff, new tool, or memory entry; a synthesis meta-agent merges the batch's proposals into the next global scaffold, dropping instance-specific edits
signatures.conditions: Verifiable tasks with executable environments; strong optimizer LLM (claude-4.5-opus); ~20 dev instances; N_max=2, batch 4
signatures.feedback: Trajectories plus unit-test/verifier outcomes on dev tasks
signatures.selection_rule_data: LLM synthesis prompt preferring multi-instance-supported changes; no scored gate or re-validation before adoption
signatures.persistence: global_v000... scaffold folders including tool directories and a static memory bank
signatures.later_use: Next batch runs on the updated scaffold; final scaffold is evaluated on held-out test instances; tools are lazily read via SKILL.md metadata
signatures.claimed_effect: Average 66.15 vs best baseline 60.62 (ExpeL), 13 settings, gpt-5-mini task agent
signatures.failure_boundary: Weak optimizer models fail to beat human-designed scaffolds; dev size sensitivity; high per-dataset creation variance

signatures.object: Evidence access for the optimizer (ReCreate-Environment per episode)
signatures.information: Episode stored as an environment with indexed critical events (errors, failing tests, file operations) linked to context
signatures.operation: Optimizer retrieves narrowing evidence on demand from outcome to relevant steps instead of reading full logs
signatures.later_use: Used by per-instance and synthesis agents
signatures.claimed_effect: Inspection dominates creation (about 65-76% of actions) and removing the trajectory is the largest observation-level ablation drop

gap.author_gap: Automated agent generation optimizes scaffolds as a black box on scalar metrics, giving no evidence about why/how agents fail and incurring high evaluation cost (ADAS ~$500 for one ARC generation with 20 tasks).
gap.checked_gap: The cost and 'metric-only' characterization is accurate for ADAS/AgentSquare/AFlow, but the paper's own related-work lists trajectory-using self-evolvers (ExpeL, AWM, SCOPE, Live-SWE-Agent), so the residue is narrower: on-demand inspection of full experience and multi-component scaffold editing from minimal seeds.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: ADAS/AFlow/AgentSquare/AgentSwift (metric-driven search) -> ScoreFlow/FlowReasoner (trained generators) -> ExpeL/AWM/Live-SWE-Agent/OPRO/TextGrad/SCOPE (experience or trace refinement of pre-existing agents) -> ReCreate. Versions as cited in paper.
gap.residue: Agent-driven white-box scaffold creation across prompt, workflow, tool and memory from minimal seeds, with batch-level generalization.
gap.stakes: Reported cost of metric-driven search (ADAS); scaffold-fixable headroom of 37 issues (20% of union) on SWE-bench Lite among five scaffolds with the same LLM (App. E).
gap.method_response: Agent-as-optimizer with experience retrieval, creation router and hierarchical updates.
gap.remaining_gap: Optimizer strength dependence, admission/rollback, harness-level adaptation, weights, larger dev sets.
unresolved: Whether baselines were given the same optimizer model and dev budget.

rs_pattern.reason: Read assumption_audit_and_pivot (its operation relaxes or violates a load-bearing assumption with proof, bound or exploit; ReCreate challenges 'scalar metric is the only signal' but executes an empirical agent loop, not a relax/violate-and-rederive step), adapt_via_conditioning with C03 (requires a canonical conditioning schema and an upstream phase with held-out task categories; ReCreate edits a persistent scaffold rather than conditioning a frozen model on a schema), and decompose_and_delegate with C25 (delegation of sub-problems to a sound solver via checkable artifacts; here the optimizer's artifacts are scaffold edits, not delegated solves). None of the 15 original cards defines diagnosing traces and patching a deployed non-weight artifact; recorded as outside_taxonomy, fully scored.

matches.condition_checks: S1 partial (evidence-retrieval narrows to failing steps but edits are scaffold-wide diffs); S3 partial (successes also learned from; no per-edit acceptance, replay or rollback); S4 met (batch synthesis over many instances, DomUpd ablation); S5 met (full trajectories and environment); S6 met (domain adapter, four domains); F2 partly (the added signal is rich evidence, but certification of edits is unchanged and absent); F5 at risk (failure assumed to originate in the scaffold)

created tools are SKILL.md-style packages and a static memory bank is written by the optimizer; quality filtering and dedup are via synthesis prompt only; F-condition: store is static, no outcome-grounded maintenance after creation

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Optimizer agent localizes failures from traces and environment, edits scaffold files, tools and memory, and replaces the incumbent scaffold with a synthesized version.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: H12 expects falsifiable predictions and promotion after replay/regression checks with rollback; ReCreate replaces the incumbent with an LLM-synthesized scaffold and no replay gate.

expectations.reason: Evidence retriever narrows to the failing step, but resulting edits are scaffold-level diffs across prompt/tool/memory, not minimal-subgraph edits.

Optimizer is told to learn from successes as well as failures, but no per-edit acceptance, regression test or rollback is described; synthesis prompt only says to keep the original rule when uncertain.

claims.text: ReCreate outperforms human-designed, self-evolving and automated agent generation baselines across 13 settings
claims.setting: gpt-5-mini task agent, claude-4.5-opus ReCreate-Agent, ~20 dev instances per domain, N_max=2, batch 4
claims.baseline_control: CoT, SBA, Self-Refine, LIVE, OPRO, ExpeL, ADAS, AgentSquare
claims.selection_vs_test: dev for creation, remaining data for testing; Math dev = AIME24, test = MATH500 topics
claims.result_denominator: Table 1 average 66.15 vs 60.62; McNemar pooled N=1681, p<1e-7 vs best of each category
claims.counterevidence: Baseline optimizer model and budgets unspecified; reasoning-level ablation shows gpt-5-mini optimizer fails to beat human-designed
claims.allowed_conclusion: With a strong optimizer model, scaffolds created by ReCreate score higher on held-out test instances than the listed baselines under author settings.

claims.text: Evolved scaffolds improve over minimal seed scaffolds
claims.setting: Seed-only vs evolved (Figure 6), Django seed vs final (App. M)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retained scaffold improves held-out performance over its seed in most domains (author report).

claims.setting: Figure 5 observation ablation; Table 2 router and DomUpd ablations
claims.result_denominator: single runs; drops of 2-3 points in Table 2
claims.counterevidence: No run-to-run variance; drops comparable to creation-run noise implied by Table 4
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directionally consistent ablation drops; magnitudes not distinguished from noise.

claims.counterevidence: ReCreate uses claude-4.5-opus; other baselines' costs omitted
claims.allowed_conclusion: Cheaper than ADAS in author's accounting; relative to other baselines unknown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A scaffold created from ~20 dev instances by a strong optimizer agent scores higher than a minimal seed and than the listed baselines on held-out test instances across 13 settings (author report, single runs, pooled McNemar significance); the contribution of the experience-driven design as distinct from optimizer strength, and of individual retained edits, is not isolated.
unresolved: Cost table for ReCreate and non-ADAS baselines

G.reason: Concrete, sourced bottleneck (scalar-score search ignores why failures happen and is costly; ADAS $500; 37-issue scaffold-fixable headroom on SWE-bench Lite) with a broad lineage across generation, trained-generator and self-evolving families; but trajectory-using neighbors (ExpeL, AWM, Live-SWE-Agent, SCOPE) blur the 'metric-only' framing and remaining-gap boundaries are generic.

M.reason: Inspect-reason-create chain, evidence retriever, creation router and instance-to-domain synthesis are reconstructable from Algorithm 1 and prompts, with ablations for trajectory, router and DomUpd and a seed control; key assumption that the optimizer's attribution is correct is not checked and the claimed advantage over simpler trajectory-based editors (ExpeL, OPRO with traces) is not tested under equal optimizer strength.

X.reason: Versioned global scaffolds, tool lazy-loading, memory read/write policy and a conflict-handling prompt are described, but there is no admission gate, replay/regression check or rollback, memory bank is static, and the retention rule is LLM synthesis; N_max=2 limits evidence of multi-round stability.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmarks with deterministic verifiers (SWE-bench Verified tests, DS-1000 executable checks, MATH answers, AppWorld state checks, DA-Code scores) and Docker execution; contamination of public benchmarks not examined and some test sets are small.

E.causality.reason: Seed control, observation- and action-level ablations and a model-swap check exist, but baselines are not shown to receive the same strong optimizer or dev budget, the paper shows that a weaker optimizer erases the advantage, and no per-edit-type (tool/memory/prompt) store-off or gate-off isolates what the retained artifact contributes.

E.holdout.reason: Explicit small dev set for creation and all remaining instances held out for testing, Math dev from a different benchmark, and dev-size/composition sensitivity; baseline dev usage and contamination are unreported and the single-case update analysis is on-dev only.

E.statistics.reason: Pooled McNemar significance (N=1681) and a three-dev-set std on SWE are reported, but main-table cells are single creation runs, per-dataset results swing by up to ~10 points across optimizer temperatures, and several test sets have 38-75 instances.

E.cost.reason: Author reports a 36%-82% lower optimization cost than ADAS in a figure and states the small dev/iteration budget, but compares with ADAS only, gives no tabulated ReCreate spend or token counts, and omits other baselines and deployed-scaffold inference cost.

rationale: Trace-inspecting optimizer evolves prompt/tools/memory; dev/test split, 13 sets, McNemar; baseline optimizer parity unstated, no admission gate.
